leverage.exposure: No leveraged position. The balance is positive and was topped up by the daily bonus this morning, so there is nothing to unwind and no zero-scoring risk. There is also no time pressure: the next lineup lock is nearly three weeks away over the international break, which is the widest safe window of the season. The one structural constraint that does bind is squad size rather than money — at exactly eleven players with a single legal formation, every improvement must be a buy followed by a sale, in that order, and the real ceiling on any buy is cash plus the one player actually sold, not the headline spending power.

binding_gap: Unchanged and still the only thing worth buying for: Sirch is the weakest fielded body by a wide margin and he is fit but out of the Elversberg side, which is the worst combination — no points and no injury discount. The standing shopping order remains open and is not duplicated this run. What has changed is the arithmetic around it. The claim that his market value is collapsing fast enough to make the replacement urgent came from reading a seven-day value change as a daily one; the true daily tick is roughly a seventh of that, and it is almost exactly offset by the daily league bonus. Measured over the two hours since the last run, the fundable envelope for his replacement moved by less than five thousand euros. It is flat, not shrinking, and it starts growing once he reaches the market floor in a little over a week. The board still offers nothing inside it: the only sub-envelope outfielders are a goalkeeper pair that is structurally impossible, two Paderborn bodies the injury table confirms are hurt, an Augsburg midfielder with a season average of one, and Wójcik, who remains under a standing avoid. The genuinely decaying asset in this squad is ter Horst, not Sirch — he sheds roughly three times as much value per day — but he is fit, starting today, and worth far more per matchday than anything affordable would replace him with, so he stays.

verdict.headline: No action needed.
verdict.detail: No action needed. The squad is exactly eleven with only one legal shape, the balance is positive, nobody is injured or suspended, and the one new listing since the last run is a fit-but-benched Paderborn attacker who fixes nothing. The substantive finding this run is not a trade — it is that the ledger's own urgency argument for refilling the Sirch slot was built on a seven-day market-value figure read as a daily one, and is therefore about seven times too large. Waiting for the right body costs essentially nothing; taking a merely-decent one early is no longer justified.

sell.reason: No sale this run, and none should be executed today before the relevant fixture has finished. The Sirch case remains right on the merits and wrong on sequence: the squad is at the floor of eleven, so selling him without a replacement already landed is a self-inflicted penalty far larger than the points he contributes. Buy first, then sell — never the other way round. ter Horst is the more valuable eventual sale because of how fast his value is falling, but he is in Paderborn's projected eleven today and produces real points, so selling him is only correct against a buy that genuinely beats him, and no such buy exists on this board.

buy.reason: Nothing. One new listing since the last run — Marino, a Paderborn attacker, priced exactly at market value. Killed on three independent grounds: the matchday-four preview leaves him out of Paderborn's projected eleven and off their absentee list, so he is a fit backup, which is precisely the problem we are trying to sell out of; his season average is barely above Sirch's own, so the swap is indistinguishable from noise; and he costs well over the non-negative envelope, meaning he could only be funded by selling a starter who scores four times what he does. Everything else on the board is already covered by a standing avoid. Hložek's listing expires early this afternoon at exactly market value, and that avoid stands unchanged — its reversal condition required a re-based scoring record, and Hoffenheim have not played yet, so nothing has changed since it was logged. One calibration note that bears directly on the refill: fresh clearings this morning show cheap bodies drawing far larger premiums than expensive ones, so the small envelope buys less player than its face value suggests, and a bid at market value on a contested cheap listing will probably lose.
